Question: Explain what makes a constitution codified rather than merely written.
Subject: codified constitution
A codified constitution is one in which the principles of a polity's governance are encompassed in a single comprehensive document, whereas a written constitution is when these principles are written down into a single document or set of legal documents. The distinction lies in whether the principles are contained within a single comprehensive document or across multiple documents. [1]
